text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The ruling Democratic Party's electoral campaign is well underway ahead of local polls without any real competition from the opposition parties, the newspaper commentary says.
- Polio vaccines may be administered in two stages to Albanians under 50. Two more people have died from polio in recent days.
- The opposition Socialist Party has started its campaign in local elections concentrating on the big cities.
- Jorgo Labovitiadhi has replaced Sotir Qirjazati as leader of the ethnic Greek association Omonia in southern Albania.
- Staff of the Miss Europe 96 beauty pageant celebrated the end of the contest with a big party at Piazza restaurant in central Tirana.
- An appartment in the south-western port city of Vlore was destroyed by 400 grams of dynamite but there were no casualties. Police do not know who was behind the attack.
- Cigarette smuggling is damaging the domestic industry. Albania imports 4,000 tonnes of cigarettes a year.
- A meeting between the government and the Independent Trade Union brought no results on compensation after recent price hikes.
- Albanian and German defence ministries are making their final preparations for the joint military exercise codenamed Mati 96.
- The Central Electoral Commission decided there will be three kinds of votes used in the October 20 local election.
- Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa starts a two-day visit to Albania.
- Geneva-based Inter-parliamentary Union has passed a resolution asking for the release of jailed Albanian opposition leader Fatos Nano.
- The Socialist Party will hold a rally on Wednesday at the Palace of Congresses to introduce its candidates for Tirana district in the local elections.
